key_insight: The paper introduces fuzzy-function programming: compiling a natural-language task description into a compact neural artifact that runs locally like a program, rather than relying on remote LLM API calls. This aims to make open-ended tasks more reproducible, private, and cost-effective.
problem_solved: It addresses tasks that are hard to express as rigid rules but are commonly outsourced to LLMs, such as log-line filtering, malformed JSON repair, and intent-based search ranking. The goal is to replace expensive, non-local API dependence with locally executable behavior.
method: Translate a natural-language specification into a learned function represented by weights.
Package the resulting model as a compact artifact that can be executed locally.
Use this paradigm, called Program-as-Weights, to implement fuzzy functions that behave like programs but are trained from specifications.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a new way to build task-specific systems that are cheaper to run, easier to deploy locally, and less dependent on external model providers. It also improves reproducibility and data locality for practical inference workloads.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: natural-language spec -> compilation/training -> program-as-weights -> local execution

paper_title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
paper_authors: Wentao Zhang, Liliana Hotsko, Woojeong Kim, Pengyu Nie, Stuart Shieber
